The Ministry of Justice and Attorney General is seeking qualified lawyers to join Public Prosecutions as Crown Prosecutors. The Government of Saskatchewan provides the services, programs and supports the people of Saskatchewan need. We deliver on the Saskatchewan Plan for Growth to build a strong economy, strong communities and strong families, ultimately building a stronger Saskatchewan. Dedicated to service excellence, we demonstrate innovation, collaboration and transparency, practice effective and accountable use of resources and promote engagement and leadership at all levels. The ministry provides a fair justice system that upholds the law and protects the rights of all individuals in Saskatchewan; promotes safe and secure communities; and provides legal and justice policy advice to government. The ministry vision is to ensure all Saskatchewan residents thrive in safe and fair communities. ABOUT THE JOB This is a unique opportunity to serve the public, promote community safety, and uphold the administration of justice in Saskatchewan. As a Crown Prosecutor, you will help deliver justice through fair, ethical and effective prosecutions. Public Prosecutions prosecutes those charged under the Criminal Code , Youth Criminal Justice Act and some provincial and federal statutes. Public Prosecutions assists in promoting safe communities through the just conclusion of criminal charges. The work offers an intellectual challenge and an opportunity to make a difference in your community. Your work as a Crown Prosecutor will be important to the community you’ll call home and those throughout the region. Under the direction of Public Prosecutions’ Head Office and a Regional Crown Prosecutor, you will be responsible for a multitude of duties and decisions. Primary duties are the carriage of criminal, quasi-criminal, and regulatory prosecutions in the Provincial Court for Saskatchewan and the Court of King’s Bench for Saskatchewan. This will include docket court work, trial work, and summary conviction appeals. Other duties include meeting and communicating with victims and witnesses, giving legal opinions, reviewing police reports, and advising police as appropriate. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in legal education in the areas of criminal law, ethics, and the criminal justice system. The hours of work can vary and include working evenings and weekends when duties require. Travel by road is required and possibly by air, with work possibly requiring overnight stays in other communities. The competitive salary will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. The successful candidate will be entitled to at least three weeks’ annual vacation, twelve scheduled days off, and statutory holidays. A full benefit package is available after six months of service. Why Join Public Prosecutions? As a Crown Prosecutor, your work directly impacts public safety and confidence in the justice system. You will be part of a team that: Delivers fair and timely access to justice. Promotes safe and secure communities. Supports victims and witnesses. Upholds the rule of law. Contributes to a stronger Saskatchewan. About Us The Ministry of Justice and Attorney General works to ensure Saskatchewan residents thrive in safe and fair communities. Public Prosecutions contributes to that vision by providing independent, fair, and effective prosecution services throughout the province. If you are a lawyer, eligible to practice in Saskatchewan, and possess a valid driver's licence, we encourage you to apply. Your legal skills can make a meaningful difference in communities across Saskatchewan.

The Clinical Manager, Nurse Practitioner Services provides provincial strategic, operational, professional practice, and human resource leadership for Nurse Practitioners within the Saskatchewan Cancer Agency. The role is accountable for workforce planning, recruitment, orientation, scheduling, performance management, succession planning, professional practice standards, service quality, and operational effectiveness. Maintaining current expertise in advanced nursing practice, the Clinical Manager provides professional practice leadership, mentorship, consultation, and oversight, and leads the development and implementation of policies, protocols, guidelines, and standard work supporting Nurse Practitioner practice. In collaboration with Medical Advisors, the Manager supports the competency assessment process and is responsible for communicating assessment outcomes and implementing corrective action plans, where required. Working collaboratively with the Director, Systemic Therapy & Outpatient Services & Chief Nursing Officer, medical and operational leaders, and interdisciplinary teams, the Clinical Manager supports high-quality, evidence-informed, patient- and family-centred oncology care across the province. The role also provides leadership in advancing advanced practice nursing and serves as a key resource for organizational and provincial initiatives impacting Nurse Practitioner practice. POSITION QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Master of Nursing – Nurse Practitioner or equivalent required. Master’s Degree in Nursing, Health Administration, Leadership, or related field considered an asset. Controlled Drug and Substance Act Module (CDSA) from Saskatchewan Polytechnic or Athabasca University. Where this is not complete, the successful candidate is required to complete within one year of date of hire to the position. Experience: Minimum 5 years’ experience as a Nurse Practitioner. Minimum 3 years’ experience as a Nurse Practitioner in oncology and/or hematology (malignant or benign) and/or palliative care preferred. Progressive leadership, supervisory, mentoring, or program leadership experience. Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS) certification. Oncology certification (CON(C)) considered an asset. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Demonstrated leadership and management skills in a healthcare environment. Strong knowledge of Nurse Practitioner scope of practice, regulation, and professional standards. Demonstrated ability to provide mentorship, coaching, and professional practice leadership. Effective communication, facilitation, and conflict resolution skills. Proven ability to lead change and implement innovative solutions. Experience developing policies, procedures, protocols, and standards. Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with physicians, nurses, leaders, and external stakeholders. Strong quality improvement and patient safety focus. Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated commitment to professional development and lifelong learning. Knowledge of culturally responsive care for First Nations and Métis peoples. Strong computer and health informatics skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a complex provincial healthcare environment.

Salary_Range: Pay Band 9, $58.11 to $66.5 (5 step range) GENERAL ACCOUNTABILITY: Reporting to the Director or Manager of Medical Physics, the Chief Medical Dosimetrist is responsible for daily planning, organizing and supervision of assigned operational aspects of the Dosimetry team within the Medical Physics Department. The Chief Medical Dosimetrist serves as point of contact for interdepartmental and extra-departmental issues pertaining to Dosimetry. The Chief Medical Dosimetrist monitors compliance with radiation therapy practice standards to ensure that high quality, safe treatment plans are accurately produced and administered to cancer patients requiring radiation therapy. The Chief Medical Dosimetrist ensures the work environment enables and supports excellence in dosimetry and promotes high quality work life and safety for Medical Dosimetrists. This position works directly with the Chief Medical Dosimetrist of the second site to ensure provincial standardization. The Chief Medical Dosimetrist assumes the responsibilities of the Medical Dosimetrist when required. The Chief Medical Dosimetrist has knowledge of the overall characteristics and clinical relevance of radiation oncology in the management of cancer or other disease processes, with special expertise in radiation therapy treatment planning. QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Bachelor degree/Diploma in Radiation Therapy Certification for Basic Life Saver (BLS)-C Canadian Dosimetry Certificate (CDC)* or Certified Medical Dosimetrist (CMD)* Graduate Level - Leadership Certificate (or equivalent) † Applicants that do not have, CDC or CMD will be required to obtain Certification within 5 years of the start date. Leadership Certificate will be required to complete a program within 2 years of the start date. Experience: Three (3) years previous experience as a qualified Medical Dosimetrist Memberships: Licensed with College of Medical Radiation Imaging Professionals Society (CMRIPS) Membership with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT) Skills: Ability to assume responsibility for work over others on a weekly basis. Strong leadership skills to manage medical dosimetry team including coaching, teaching, mentoring, giving effective feedback and supporting the staff through change. Expertise in the technical aspects of radiation oncology and medical physics to develop optimal treatment plans. Expert working knowledge of radiation therapy and treatment planning software systems. Knowledgeable in the areas of anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical oncology, radiobiology, radiation physics, and radiation safety. Knowledgeable in health care informatics - including the resources, devices, and methods to acquire, store and retrieve data. Displays mathematical skills including algebra, trigonometry, and introductory calculus. Competence in the use of basic office software such as Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, WebEx, and Outlook. Competence in the development and use of clinical guidelines. Possess good communication and interpersonal skills to support the exchange of information with patients, family members, and the radiation oncology treatment team as well as outside entities Strong communication skills required to develop and present complex information in written documentation and verbal presentations. Includes facilitating meetings for multidisciplinary groups. Demonstrates high-level critical thinking and problem-solving skills, to include the ability to make quick evaluation and decisions for on-line adaptive responsibilities. Works independently, but in collaboration with the radiation oncologist, medical physicist and others. Human relations skills required to ensure compliance and promote acceptance through negotiating with staff and/or suppliers where there is a requirement to resolve the conflict or situation. Accuracy of fine motor movement is required to perform detailed outlining of anatomical structures using the computer mouse. Knowledge of culturally responsive care for First Nations and Métis people.

The professional will provide psychological assessment, consultation and treatment to families whose children present with a range of mental health presentation. Will provide expert consultation to other clinicians, child/youth serving agencies, and will mentor/supervise psychologists. Assist with program development and implementation. This is a position with the Young Offender Team that treats youth affected by the Youth Criminal Justice Act. Education Recognized PhD or Master's Degree in Psychology is required. Registered or eligible for registration as a psychologist by the Saskatchewan College of Psychologists, with Authorized Practice Endorsement. Experience Requires a minimum of three years (postgraduate) recent recognized clinical experience in a community mental health setting working with children, youth and families presenting with acute and chronic mental health and addiction problems. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Extensive knowledge of normal child and adolescent and young adult development and psychopathology. Comprehensive knowledge of best practice or empirically based models for the range of childhood mental health disorders. Knowledge of and experience utilizing standardized psychometric instruments and a wide range of measures typically used with children and youth. Demonstrated ability to identify, implement and evaluate areas of client difficulty across a wide range of clinical presentation and formulate evidence based intervention. Knowledge of the diversity of cultures, values and traditions and their impact on accessing mental health services and assessment. Knowledge and demonstrated application of a variety of intervention strategies (individual and group) for children/youth with mental health and addiction problems in a community setting, including, but not limited to: assessment, triage, treatment and case management. Ability and professional maturity to develop and maintain relationships within a multidisciplinary team, interagency programs and across the community of human services. Solid consultation skills and demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with community partners and possess a broad knowledge of community resources including treatment programs and support agencies. Ability to provide public education regarding children and youth and mental health concerns. Ability to design, initiate and conduct in service training for other professionals. Ability to work independently and as a member of an interdisciplinary mental health and addiction team. Demonstrated ability to engage in community program consultation and resource development within the community. Ability to manage a complex caseload with multiple demands. Knowledge of mentoring principles and ability to provide supervision to students and peer consultation to a multidisciplinary team. Knowledge and practical application of the Mental Health Services Act and Health Information Protection Act and other legislation that impacts the work of clinicians in a mental health and addiction setting. Strong communication skills (written and verbal). Ability to document and complete psychological reports in a concise and timely manner. Excellent interpersonal competence including effective problem solving and conflict resolution skills, and an ability to respond under pressure. Ability to enter and retrieve data in computer database systems. This position will work in an 18-unit transitional apartment setting with Relatives who have recently been released from a correctional facility or are on Probation. The incumbent uses evaluation techniques to develop and implement therapeutic treatment plans as a part of the case planning process. Plan and administer therapeutic treatment to Relatives which includes providing individual and group therapy as needed. Change methods and degree of therapy when indicated by Relative’s reactions. Monitor Relative’s treatment progress and keep track of their mental status. Aid Relatives’ in maintaining mental health stability. Refer Relatives to supportive services to supplement treatment and counseling. Develop annual comprehensive mental health assessment for Relative’s under the direct care. Provide crisis intervention consultation to all members of the team. May conduct research in treatment and test validation. May develop evaluative studies of therapy and therapy outcome. Document medical records according to requirements of regulatory agencies. Maintain written records of all Relative interactions. Complete annual training required for positions such as crisis intervention training. Maintain confidentiality of records relating to Relatives and treatment plans at all times. Act as a patient advocate to coordinate required services or to resolve emergency problems in crisis situations. SaskTel is seeking an experienced Construction Project Manager to lead major infrastructure projects. This person will oversee large-scale construction initiatives from inception to completion. They will be responsible for managing all phases of projects including—planning, procurement, execution, and close-out—while coordinating internal teams, external consultants, and key stakeholders. In this role, you will: Lead the delivery of complex commercial construction projects with significant organizational impact. Manage budgets, schedules, and risk mitigation strategies to ensure successful outcomes. Provide strategic oversight and reporting to the program manager. Ensure quality, safety, and compliance standards are met at every stage. If you have a proven track record in delivering major construction projects, strong leadership capabilities, and a passion for driving excellence—we want to hear from you! GENERAL ACCOUNTABILITY Accountable for the successful delivery and execution of large-scale capital construction and renovation projects from detailed design through occupancy and project closeout. Responsible for owner-side management of the physical construction of assigned projects, ensuring scope, schedule, budget, quality, safety, and operational requirements are achieved. Provides oversight and direction to design consultants, construction managers, contractors, and specialty consultants throughout all phases of project delivery. Acts as the primary owner representative during design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover, ensuring all project activities align with approved program objectives, corporate standards, regulatory requirements, and operational needs. Works closely with the Program Manager to manage project-level risks, issues, stakeholder expectations, and change requests while maintaining continuity of business operations throughout construction activities. SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES 1. Project Planning & Development • Leads project planning activities including scope definition, budget development, scheduling, risk identification, procurement planning, phasing strategies, occupancy coordination, and project execution planning. • Coordinates design development activities to ensure project requirements, operational needs, technical standards, and stakeholder expectations are incorporated into project documents. • Ensures construction planning considers business continuity, occupant impacts, safety requirements, and operational constraints. 2. Design Consultant Management • Directs and manages architectural, engineering, and specialty design consultants throughout project development and delivery. • Reviews and coordinates design submissions to ensure compliance with project objectives, technical standards, budget constraints, and schedule requirements. • Facilitates design reviews and constructability reviews with stakeholders and subject matter experts. • Manages consultant contracts, deliverables, performance, and compliance with contractual obligations. 3. Construction Manager & Contractor Oversight • Acts as the primary owner representative for construction activities. • Provides oversight of the Construction Manager and contractors to ensure project objectives are achieved. • Reviews and monitors construction plans, schedules, resource plans, procurement activities, and site performance. • Coordinates resolution of construction issues and field conditions. • Ensures compliance with contract requirements, safety regulations, quality standards, and approved project documentation. 4. Construction Execution & Coordination • Oversees construction activities to ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with approved plans and specifications. • Coordinates demolition, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, telecommunications, security, and specialty system work. • Ensures effective integration and sequencing of multiple trades and work packages. • Facilitates coordination between contractors, occupants, operational groups, and technical stakeholders. 5. Contract Administration • Administers construction and consultant contracts in accordance with corporate policies and approved procurement strategies. • Reviews and recommends approvals for change orders, progress claims, contingency usage, and contract amendments. • Maintains appropriate records and documentation to support contractual requirements and decision-making. 6. Financial Management • Accountable for project budgets, forecasts, cash flow management, contingency control, and financial reporting. • Monitors project costs and proactively identifies variances, risks, and mitigation opportunities. • Ensures expenditures align with approved project authority and funding allocations. 7. Schedule Management • Develops and maintains project schedules and milestone tracking. • Monitors progress against approved schedules and implements recovery strategies when required. • Coordinates critical project activities to minimize impacts to cost, quality, and operational requirements. 8. Risk & Change Management • Identifies, evaluates, and manages project risks throughout the project lifecycle. • Implements mitigation plans and escalates significant risks as appropriate. • Administers project change management processes for scope, schedule, budget, and design changes. • Assesses impacts and develops recommendations to support informed decision-making. 9. Quality Assurance & Commissioning • Ensures quality management processes are implemented throughout design and construction. • Oversees inspections, testing, commissioning, deficiency management, and project closeout activities. • Verifies systems and facilities perform as intended and meet operational requirements. 10. Health, Safety & Regulatory Compliance • Promotes and supports a strong safety culture throughout all project activities. • Ensures compliance with applicable legislation, building codes, regulatory requirements, and corporate safety standards. • Monitors contractor safety performance and addresses concerns promptly. 11.Stakeholder Management & Communication • Maintains strong relationships with project stakeholders, business units, technical authorities, consultants, contractors, and regulatory agencies. • Provides regular project reporting on status, risks, budget, schedule, and key decisions. • Facilitates project meetings and supports stakeholder engagement activities. • Communicates impacts, risks, and construction activities effectively to affected groups. 12.Project Closeout & Occupancy • Coordinates commissioning, training, occupancy planning, turnover documentation, warranties, and post-occupancy support. • Ensures project documentation is complete and deficiencies are resolved prior to project closure. • Leads lessons learned reviews and supports continuous improvement initiatives. QUALIFICATIONS 1. Degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or a post-secondary Project Management program, or related discipline and/or equivalent experience. 2. Project Management Professional (PMP®) designation preferred. 3. Minimum 5 years of experience managing complex commercial, institutional, or industrial construction projects, including major renovations and occupied-building projects. 4. Demonstrated experience managing design consultants, construction managers, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams. 5. Strong knowledge of construction delivery methods, including Construction Management, Design-Bid-Build, and Design-Build. 6. Experience with contract administration, procurement, cost control, scheduling, commissioning, and construction project governance. 7. Strong understanding of building systems including architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and specialty systems. 8. Demonstrated experience managing projects in operational environments with significant stakeholder coordination requirements. 9. Excellent negotiation, communication, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills. 10.Proven ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining schedule, budget, quality, and safety objectives.
